newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures trade mixed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures trade mixed.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed Wednesday, with California Oregon Border (COB) front month down slightly at values that several traders felt may maintain their strength, sources said.
"This market seems to be relatively well valued," said one New York based futures trader.
As of 1300 EST, March COB was down 12 cents at $11.00, while April COB was bid at $9.85 and offered at $10.15 per megawatt hour (MWh) from Tuesday's settle at $10.25.
March Palo Verde (PV) was trading steady at $13.65 after exchanges as low as $13.65 per MWh, while April PV was trading up five cents at $12.35 per MWh following exchanges as low as $12.30.

Some possible downward pressure was seen from abundant hydroelectric supplies in the Pacific Northwest, but that pressure was likely being offset by firming cash power prices and a rebound in natural gas futures, the sources said.
NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures were trading down 6.2 cents at $2.435 per million British thermal units.
NYMEX said as of 1235 EST an estimated total of 137 COB and 35 PV contracts had traded.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average two to four degrees Fahrenheit above normal in northern areas and three to six degrees above normal in southern areas late this week, although temperatures were called to drop to near normal over the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to stay two to four degrees below normal through the same period due to clouds and light precipitation.
Bonneville Power Administration said it was raising the price of offers for firm, heavy load power for Thursday delivery by $3.00 to $16.00 per MWh in the Northwest.
Separately, a 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut last Saturday for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for up to two weeks.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., boosted its output to 68 percent capacity from Tuesday's 59 percent following work on its recirculation pumps.
COB open interest for Feb 4 rose 82 to 3,600, while PV open interest rose 12 to 1,398, NYMEX said.
